Briefing on disk at docs/federation/OPENCODE_DB_MANAGEMENT_BRIEFING.md (9 sections, 23K, 35 cited URLs). Three headline items: (1) I retract an earlier wrong 46GB scan estimate — it used file size instead of searchable row count (~4.9 µs/row measured); (2) read-only access to a WAL DB is conditional in SQLite 3.22.0+ and the immutable=1 fallback returns stale data — hence two independent safety layers in ocdb-ro; (3) schema drift is live and the popular community schema doc is already wrong for this host (session.data does not exist), with four documented upstream migration incidents in 2026 including one where opencode2 mutated the shared production DB in place.
context:
Full briefing with all 35 source URLs is on disk at docs/federation/OPENCODE_DB_MANAGEMENT_BRIEFING.md (9 sections, 23K). Summary of what it contains and the three things that change your plan:

=== 1. RETRACTION OF AN EARLIER WRONG NUMBER ===
I previously told you "46 GB → ~64 s per query." That multiplied 1.4 ms/MB by FILE SIZE — the wrong denominator. File size is dominated by `tool` blobs; on Node 1 a 1.9 GB file held only 14.3 MB of searchable text. The real measured rate is ~4.9 µs/row (58,612 parts → 282 ms scan). USE THE SEARCHABLE ROW COUNT, not the file size. §1 has the queries.

=== 2. READ-ONLY ON WAL IS NOT SIMPLE ===
SQLite only relaxed "cannot open read-only WAL databases" in 3.22.0, and only if the -shm/-wal already exist, OR the directory is writable, OR you use `immutable`. Source: sqlite.org/wal.html §4. The forum is blunter (sqlite.org/forum/info/0667868158167ccb): "A LOGICAL (ie, application level) read-only connection is still required to have PHYSICAL (ie, Operating System level) write-access to the SHM file." And: "If the database is immutable and nonetheless is 'mutated', all hell will break loose."
At 46 GB your DB will get archived/moved/opened by a non-owner, where a tool that assumes it can create -shm will fail — and the fallback `immutable=1` returns STALE data (measured 26 parts behind). This is why ocdb-ro carries two independent layers: statement allowlist AND engine-level sqlite3 -readonly + mode=ro. Verified 9/9 legit reads pass, 13/13 adversarial writes blocked, sandbox sha256 byte-identical, and bypassing the text filter still hits "attempt to write a readonly database" at the engine.

=== 3. SCHEMA DRIFT IS LIVE AND THE COMMUNITY DOC IS WRONG ===
The most-cited opencode schema reference (github.com/madcat-archive/opencode/reference/opencode-sqlite-schema.md) documents `session.data` as a JSON blob. THAT COLUMN DOES NOT EXIST on this host — the live `session` table is flat columns (version, project_id, workspace_id, path, metadata, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read/write, revert, permission). Any tool written against that doc will fail. Node 1 today: 38 rows in `migration`, latest 20260622202450_simplify_session_input, no __drizzle_migrations, no *_v2 tables — clean V1 install.
Upstream migration incidents in 2026: #36407 (legacy drizzle break, TUI swallows the error and appears to hang), #34584 (duplicate column cost), #33898 (migrations break DOWNGRADE — no such column: replacement_seq), #42260 (opencode2 migrated the SHARED opencode.db in place, broke stable 1.x with `no such table: session_context_epoch` while integrity_check still said ok — drift, not corruption; fixed by isolating the preview's namespace). Also #41217: V2 writes session_v2 and never imports V1 history, so V1 sessions go invisible with no supported migration path.

=== ALSO IN THE BRIEFING ===
• The correct staleness-free FTS5 mechanism: external-content table + triggers, with the three documented gotchas — triggers DO NOT backfill (run 'rebuild'), rowid must be set explicitly or you get "unsafe use of virtual table" (FTS5 looks up as SELECT cols FROM content WHERE content_rowid=?), and use BEFORE UPDATE not AFTER or stale tokens survive forever. Plus: never write triggers into the PRODUCTION db — do it in a separate index db with a high-water-mark staleness check on MAX(part.time_created).
• Safe live backup: `VACUUM INTO '/backup/x.db'` or `.backup '/backup/x.db'`. Never `cp` a live WAL database (sqlite.org/backup.html: power failure mid-copy can corrupt the backup). Also capture the -wal sidecar (95 MB on Node 1).
• Concurrency, measured: 0 SQLITE_BUSY across 50 rapid reads against a live writer; snapshot-stable. But PRAGMA busy_timeout is 0 here, and checkpoint starvation (wal.html §6) means don't hold a read txn open across a long scan on 46 GB.
• SQLite max DB is ~17.5 TB at default page size (sqlite.org/limits.html) — 46 GB is a performance problem, not a format ceiling.
• 3-tier decision table by searchable row count: <200k = no index; 200k–2M = FTS5 sidecar; >2M = sidecar + month partitioning.
• 9 rejected tools with reasons. All OpenCode FTS plugins lose on the same axis: the plugin runtime is embedded Bun 1.2 (node:sqlite absent, verified live), and bun:sqlite REJECTS URI filenames (file:...?mode=ro → "unable to open database file"), so plugins are forced onto the weaker readonly:true form.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT DO ===
No shell on Node 0 — Tailscale ACL blocks SSH on :22, and hub TLS fails verification from Node 1. The federation diagnosed PASS on all five checks, so the mesh is healthy; I just have no command path. Every Node 0 figure in the briefing is a projection and is labelled UNMEASURED in §6. Run §1 and the row counts will settle the tier.
